A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, figures, equations, references, and Appendices A-D. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-connectivity experiments with trained transformers and three reasoning LLMs, reinforcement-learning results, and additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original graph and reinforcement-learning experiments and additionally reports s1-32B results on AIME2024.

M1.justification: The CoT strategies, transformer architectures, verification and aggregation rules, budget forcing, and STaR procedure are unchanged. The AIME2024 experiment evaluates an existing model and scaling approach rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic bridge and two-path graph-connectivity tasks. v2 retains these and adds competition mathematics through s1-32B evaluation on AIME2024 (Section 4.5, Figure 12), substantially broadening coverage beyond graph connectivity.

E2.justification: The retained graph comparisons use the same CoT strategies, majority-vote and best-of-n methods, and three reasoning LLMs. The added AIME experiment reuses s1-32B and the existing sequential-versus-majority-vote comparison without introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: The added AIME protocol evaluates token budgets from 0.5K to 16K and parallel sample counts from 1 to 64, using temperature 1.0 and majority voting (Figure 12). The samples-to-exceed-95%-accuracy evaluation disappears with v1 Figure 13. Settings for the retained graph experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 Figure 13's analysis of how many parallel samples are needed to exceed 95% accuracy as bridge depth increases is removed. The CoT-strategy, Walk-L budget, smaller-transformer/DFS-BT, and RL-iteration analyses remain, including figures relocated within the appendices.

E5.justification: v2 removes Figure 5's caption statement identifying its unchanged error bars as 95% binomial confidence intervals. Removing v1 Figure 13 also removes its five-run-average disclosure. Other confidence-interval conventions and the graph-LLM standard-deviation bound remain; this does not establish fewer runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds the s1-32B AIME accuracy grid, showing limited compensation from parallel sampling at short sequential budgets, and removes v1 Figure 13's sample-count results. Matched graph and RL results are unchanged, including the Bridge(3) evidence-accuracy increase from 21.16% to 92.02% after four RL iterations.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects Lemma 1's accumulated-error factor from p1(n) to p2(n), and Theorem 4's bounded event from an incorrect answer to a correct answer. Its proof also adds explicit approximation/triangle-inequality steps and majority-gate composition. The theorem set and central assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 broadens the claimed empirical contribution from graph-connectivity validation to a consistent sequential-scaling advantage on AIME2024 as well. The central theoretical separation and emergent longer-CoT claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly interprets AIME results as supporting generalization to real-world mathematical reasoning, while stating that quantifying the exact trade-off there is beyond scope. The existing limitations about task dependence, model optimality, and the heuristic status of VQM remain in Section 6.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds AIME hardware and runtime information: H200 GPUs, approximately 1.5 hours per run, and about 24 H200 GPU-hours total. Existing graph implementation details are retained. The same code link moves from a footnote to the abstract without changing access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds the AIME2024 source citation [oA24]. The other cited works and Appendix D's positioning relative to transformer expressivity, inference-time scaling, and reinforcement-learning research remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local prose edits, standardizes heading capitalization, shortens Section 6's title to Discussion, and updates author/contact and acknowledgment text. Sections 1.1 and 4.5 expand locally, while the overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the AIME heatmap, removes v1 Figure 13, and relocates the unchanged budget-trade-off plots from main-text Figure 6 to appendix Figure 8. Several other figures are repositioned or renumbered, and Figure 5's caption is shortened. Retained plot designs and graphical results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The AIME experiment provides a useful empirical check beyond the synthetic graph setting, and Appendix A corrects specific mathematical inconsistencies. These modest gains outweigh the loss of the sample-efficiency plot and some statistical documentation. The improvement is limited by sparse AIME protocol and uncertainty reporting; the revision does not establish broad generalization or fully repair the existing proof's approximation argument.
